For the seven V2 secondary-output tests, the AC supply reported input real
power \(P_{\mathrm{in}}\), and the electronic load reported voltage and current
at its input terminals. The secondary power estimate was
\(P_{\mathrm{sec}}=V_{\mathrm{load}}I_{\mathrm{load}}\), giving an efficiency
estimate of \(100P_{\mathrm{sec}}/P_{\mathrm{in}}\) percent. The supply and
load readings in each capture share a recorded timestamp; hardware
synchronization and averaging intervals were not specified. The estimate
therefore applies to the captured operating point and includes the output
cable loss between the converter and load.
reason: Defines the new test measurement locations, calculation and timing limitation alongside the existing general method.

new:
For the seven V2 load tests, region R3 covered the input bridge and R1
covered the secondary. The reported values are the maximum apparent surface
temperatures within those regions. The regions displayed an emissivity of
0.95; the camera footer displayed 0.97. The camera timestamps follow the
same sequence as the electrical captures, with a one-hour clock offset and
approximately 2--4 seconds between paired timestamps. The clocks were not
shown to be synchronized. None of these tests reached thermal stability.

Ambient, airflow, warm-up, and camera setup were not fully recorded.
The identified hotspots can be monitored during longer runs.
reason: Defines the region readings and records the distinct camera settings and timing needed to interpret the new thermal sequence.
facts_preserved: R3 input bridge and R1 secondary as confirmed by user
ROI emissivity 0.95 and footer 0.97 are distinct
Electrical and camera clocks are not established as synchronized
